page: Microsoft Azure D4ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DADSv5 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The server features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory allocation stands at 16.0 GB of RAM, translating to 4.0 GB per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 154 GB SSD, and it supports Premium Storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile for the D4ads_v5. Single-core CPU performance is a notable strength, with stress-ng single-core benchmarks placing it in the top 25% with a score of 2700.19. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show limitations. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block speeds at 38.0 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 22.11 GB/sec, both categorized in the bottom 25%. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression drops to the bottom 10%.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, the D4ads_v5 is suited for workloads that rely on single-thread performance rather than highly parallelized computing. Appropriate workloads include basic web serving, text processing, and light utility operations, though Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations both rank in the bottom 25%. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of a dedicated AMD EPYC processor and a local 154 GB SSD provides a balanced resource density for general-purpose utility tasks that do not require high memory bandwidth or intensive multi-core scaling.
